clue.text: Latinate construction put up in garden

definitions.text: Latinate construction put up in garden

parts.words: Latinate construction put up in garden
parts.note: the summerhouse's name is a mock-Latin coinage meaning 'I shall gaze', so it is a Latin-style word construction as well as a garden building

explanation.walkthrough: 'Construction' works twice: a word built like Latin, and a structure erected in a garden. The word is jokey pseudo-Latin formed on 'gaze'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small open-sided garden pavilion with a view, whose name was coined as fake Latin.

clue.text: Deny game is fixed for cupholder

indicators.note: a fixed game is rigged, so the letters of deny game are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone denies that a match was rigged to win a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cupholder' suggests a trophy winner; in myth he was the cupbearer to the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Trojan youth served as cupbearer to Zeus on Olympus.

clue.text: Many taken sick in part of Jerusalem

indicators.note: in places the word for sick inside the name of the hill

parts.note: Zion is the hill in Jerusalem on which the city of David stood
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Many people have been taken ill in an area of Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: A zillion is an informal word for an enormous, indefinite number.

clue.text: Butterfly fills up time with a joke

parts.note: brims means fills to the top
one is a joke, as in 'have you heard the one about...'

explanation.surface: A butterfly fills the time with a funny story.
explanation.definitionFit: The brimstone is a pale yellow European butterfly.

clue.text: Fragrant wood beside main road — cedars, primarily

parts.note: balsa is a very light tropical wood
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: primarily means take only the first letter of the word cedars

explanation.surface: A scented timber sits next to a busy highway lined with cedar trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, its 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something balmy and aromatic, like resin or the vinegar named for it, is fragrant.

clue.text: We grace a dinner cooked for philanthropist

indicators.note: cooked means doctored, so the letters of we grace a dinner are reworked

explanation.surface: We say grace before a dinner prepared for a wealthy benefactor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish-American steel magnate gave away most of his fortune, funding libraries and foundations.

clue.text: Black book put in auction

indicators.note: put in tells us the letter for book is placed inside the word for auction

parts.note: a sale is an auction

explanation.surface: A black-bound volume is entered in an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic term for black, and a poetic word for it.

clue.text: Mother's pet dog

parts.note: ma's is mother's
a pet is a fit of sulking, as is a tiff, a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Mum's favourite pet is a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is not an animal but a sulk, 'in a pet'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff is a large, powerful breed of dog.

clue.text: Short of cash, laboriously climb slope

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the cash abbreviation is removed from the verb

parts.note: to clamber is to climb with effort
L stands for pound, the money sign

explanation.surface: Broke, someone struggles up a steep incline.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for the pound sterling, so for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is the slight slope or curve across a road surface.

clue.text: Pious gesture used in addition?

parts.note: a Christian blessing made with the hand, which is also the plus symbol used in sums

explanation.definitionFit: Tracing a cross over the body is a devout gesture, and + marks addition.

clue.text: Cancelled out zero, even though that is 500

parts.note: null means nothing, zero
if can mean even though, as in 'pleasant if dull'
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone's sums come out at nothing, though really they made five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify something is to make it void, invalidating or cancelling it.

clue.text: It's necessary to describe some thing as cleaner

annotationWithheld.why: 'It's necessary to describe some thing as cleaner': the letters sit in 'describe some', but no word in the clue as held signals a hidden word, so the parse cannot be given honestly; possibly an OCR or setter slip.
annotationWithheld.clue: It's necessary to describe some thing as cleaner

clue.text: China's nemesis after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so the letters of nemesis are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: China's downfall comes at the hands of a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After revolution' signals an anagram of NEMESIS, not a simple reversal; 'China' is porcelain, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen is a German town famous for its fine porcelain, often called Dresden china.

clue.text: Recluse before acquiring a little money

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a very small sum of money, as in the widow's mite

explanation.surface: A hermit who once had nothing comes into a small sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit living in solitude for religious reasons is a recluse.

clue.text: Ring round wild animal

parts.note: a din is a loud ringing noise
a go is a turn or round, as in a game

explanation.surface: An animal handler circles a wild beast in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian wild dog is a feral wild animal.

clue.text: A means of smoothing brought about, in fact

annotationWithheld.why: 'A means of smoothing brought about, in fact' as held lacks fodder: FACT round an anagram of LIFE would give the answer, but no word LIFE (or similar) is in the clue, so a word appears to be missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: A means of smoothing brought about, in fact

clue.text: Oil unusual in Art Club

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of in and art club come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd oil painting appears in the art club's show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil' suggests a painting; here it is a substance that reduces friction.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is the standard example of a substance that lessens friction between parts.

clue.text: Make a living before business, we hear, is sold

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: be (exist, live) comes before trade (business)

explanation.surface: Earning a living ahead of a business deal is a sell-out.
explanation.walkthrough: BE + TRADE, said out, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sold out, as by a traitor, is to be double-crossed.

clue.text: Got round number organised

indicators.note: round signals that the letters of got are brought about into another order

parts.note: ether, the old anaesthetic, is something that numbs, a 'number'

explanation.surface: Someone collected a figure and put it in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is read as 'something that numbs': ETHER. The letters of 'Got' rearranged give TOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A together person is calm and well organised, in informal usage.

clue.text: Bowling by member in the usual style

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowls with a normal action.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is six consecutive balls from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowling in cricket is normally done with the arm above the shoulder, the standard way.

clue.text: Russian poet joined by English fellow

parts.note: Alexander Blok was a Russian Symbolist poet

explanation.surface: A Russian poet teams up with an English companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloke is British slang for a man or chap.

clue.text: Express preference for one state of light

parts.note: to opt is to choose
I is the Roman numeral one
Cal is the abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Someone chooses one American state for its light.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to sight and visible light.

clue.text: Thus whales seen after one crustacean

indicators.note: after says the pieces for thus and whales follow the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means thus
a pod is a group of whales

explanation.surface: Thus whales are spotted following a lone creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodlice and their relatives are small flattened crustaceans of this order.

clue.text: Woman will account for the varnish

parts.note: she'll is the contraction of she will

explanation.surface: A woman promises to explain where the varnish went.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin from lac insects used to make a glossy varnish.

clue.text: Alloy that's strange but true

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of alloy are in an odd, unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: A metal mixture sounds odd but genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: A faithful, steadfast supporter is true to the cause.

clue.text: He puts out English champion

parts.note: a victor is a winner or champion

explanation.surface: A sportsman knocks out the English title-holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who expels a tenant turns them out of the property.

clue.text: Derbyshire is not healthy

definitions.meaning: the county contains the Peak District, so it is hilly, full of peaks
British informal for looking pale and unwell

explanation.surface: A Midlands county is said to be in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: DERBYSHIRE is an English county whose hilly north is the Peak District; the first sense reads it as 'peak-filled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaky describes someone sickly and pale, and also hilly land with many summits.

clue.text: Not many make it, as a rule

definitions.text: Not many make it, as a rule

parts.words: Not many make it, as a rule
parts.note: reads as a remark about rare success, but describes a system in which a small few hold power and govern

explanation.definitionFit: This is government by a small group, so a few people form the ruling body.

clue.text: Political protest by left is hard to break up

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration, a political protest
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A left-wing demonstration proves difficult for police to disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: To raze a building is to knock it down and break it apart.

clue.text: Only a short time in firm and showing little interest

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for firm

parts.note: solid means firm
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone joins a company only briefly and stays indifferent.
explanation.definitionFit: An impassive, unemotional person shows little feeling or curiosity.
